description: Golden corpus for credential-entry.v1; the single inventory read by Go, Python and ajv (G-70). A reject_by_client entry with `after` is a TRANSITION from that accepted entry; without it, it is a single-document client rule. clock_now is the instant status is checked against.

accept.why: Only the required members: no fingerprint (a row that predates migration 0007), no expiry, no creator, empty sets.
Expired: expires_at is required and lies before the manifest clock.
Revoked: revoked_at and a reason code.
A metadata projection of an ACR credential: names its domain record. ACR stays the validator (ACP-ADR-08).
A rotated credential names its parent and narrows its scopes.

reject.why: No id.
Status is derived but always on the wire: a reader must not recompute it.
A status outside the closed vocabulary.
Revoked requires revoked_at and a reason (here revoked_at is missing).
An active credential carrying revoked_at: status and timestamps must agree.
Expired requires expires_at.
A secret value in a registry entry: unrepresentable, not merely optional (TRD section 12). THE load-bearing rejection.
The stored verifier is not a wire member either.
A token member.
17 characters: the prefix length is pinned at 16 by the schema, not left to a producer.
A space in the prefix.
Scopes have principal.v1's colon-separated shape.
Scopes are a set.
66 characters: the database caps a scope at 64.
17 audiences.
Unknown credential class denies.
Fingerprints are 16 lowercase hex characters.
A projected credential names its domain record.
A platform credential has no domain record to name.
The database column is free text; the wire form is a reason code, never prose or an address.
An id with another aggregate's prefix.
Hour 24.

reject_by_client.why: Lexically valid, no such day: every client refuses it (the shared timestamp rule).
UTC year 0000: the shared timestamp rule refuses it.
Status says active but expires_at is before the manifest clock: the schema pins the shape, only a clock can check it.
Status says expired but expires_at is in the future.
THE lifecycle rule (TRD section 12, revocation is monotonic): after valid-revoked.json the same credential is active again. Schema-valid by itself; refused as a transition.
A revoked credential's revoked_at moved later: revocation is idempotent, the original instant stands.
The reason of a revocation rewritten.
A scope added in place: privilege narrows or stays, it never widens in place.
A credential's class changed in place.
The fingerprint replaced under the same id: verifier-adjacent identity is immutable (a new secret is a rotation).

A credential that is its own rotation parent: schema-valid (two well-formed crd_ ids), impossible lineage; the producer refuses it (CHECK credential_registry_not_its_own_parent), so every client must.
